entries.title: You can officially buy the Pixel 11 phones and Pixel Watch 5.

entries.title: 5 ways to upgrade your home decor with Google Search
entries.summary: Illustration of ombre rainbow furniture items like a sofa, lamp, and chair against a purple background
entries.content:
People turn to Google Search every day for discovery and inspiration, including when it comes to home decor: Searches for “home decor inspo” are up 300% in the past month, and both “bathroom inspo” and “living room inspo” are breakout searches in the same timeframe. Bold pops of color are in, too — this year's trending paint searches include teal and magenta.

Getting inspired is the fun part. Making your vision reality is where people can get stuck. Here are five ways you can use Google Search tools to take action on your home decor vision board.

1. Visualize furniture in your space.

When you're eyeing a new couch or other large piece of furniture, it can be hard to know if the piece will actually fit your room both physically and aesthetically. AI Mode in Search can help you visualize it so you feel more confident about what will work in your space. Simply upload a photo of your room and ask something like, "Based on my living room, what kind of couch would you recommend? The wall is 84 inches wide." You can then see inspiration for different types of couches that would fit in that spot and follow up with a prompt like, "Can you show me what an emerald green velvet sofa could look like?" to see a mockup right in your space.

2. Learn more and shop decor with Lens in Search.

This year, people are searching for vintage more than ever before, with “vintage braided rugs” and “vintage wood coffee table” as the top trending home furnishing items. If you're out and about and see a vintage decorative item you love, you can use Google Lens to learn more about it and find similar items online within your price range. Just take a picture of the item with the Google app on iOS or Android, and Lens will pull up links to similar items so you can bring that vintage style home.

3. Uncover new decor finds with Circle to Search.

Sometimes online scrolling leads to the best discoveries. With Circle to Search, you can track down the decor you love — from videos, social feeds, or web pages — without switching apps. Spot a social post featuring fish wallpaper (searches are up 140% in the past month!) that would look perfect in your home? Just long press the home button or navigation bar on the latest Pixel and Samsung Galaxy S26 devices, then circle the wallpaper on your screen to see similar options or ask a question about the product.

4. Tackle DIY projects with Search Live.

Let’s say you’re one of the many people searching for floating shelves (a top-trending item this year) to put in your new studio apartment. They’re cute and practical — but once you buy them, you still have to install them. Search Live can help guide you through DIY projects step-by-step. To get started, just open the Google app and tap the Live icon under the search bar. You can start asking your questions out loud like you’re talking to a friend and enable video input to share visual context from your camera feed to get the job done right.

5. Get a great price.

Getting your home just-right can add up. Before you buy that funky lamp or harlequin wallpaper (both breakout searches in the past month), do a quick price check to make sure you’re getting a good deal. Just tap on any product listing to compare costs across stores. You can also expand the typical price drop down to view price history and get a sense of whether the current listing is high, low, or typical. Still not ready to buy? Tap “Track price” and you’ll get an alert when it falls into your budget.

entries.title: Here’s how to use intelligent dictation in Gemini for macOS.
entries.summary: Enable Google’s new intelligent dictation feature in the Gemini app for macOS and speak naturally into any window on your desktop.
entries.content:
We recently introduced a new way to create, edit, and summarize in the Gemini app for macOS using just your voice, right where you’re already working. This intelligent dictation feature allows you to speak naturally into any window on your desktop, transcribing your spoken words into clean, polished text. It automatically removes the “ums” and “ahs,” catches mid-sentence corrections, and drops the formatted text instantly at your cursor.

See this feature in action — and learn how to turn it on — in the video below.

entries.content:

We’re bringing Google Play Points to life with The Quest, an interactive treasure hunt where participants can complete challenges to unlock access to a gacha machine packed with more than 53,000 prizes. Attendees can climb the live Play League leaderboard in high-stakes tournaments and create custom profile avatars at the photo booth, while Diamond+ members can unwind in our exclusive MVP Lounge.

entries.title: We’re partnering with the State of Delaware to provide free AI and career training.
entries.summary: Google partners with Delaware to provide free Career Certificates and AI training to residents statewide.
entries.content:
We’re working alongside the Delaware Department of Labor and Delaware Libraries to provide residents with no-cost access to Google Career Certificates and Google AI courses. This initiative helps Delawareans gain valuable, high-demand skills for today’s fast-growing careers, with no college degree or previous experience required.

The flexible, self-paced online training programs include:

  • Google AI courses: Foundational offerings, including the Google AI Professional Certificate that help residents learn to use AI tools to boost everyday workplace productivity, write effective prompts, and build custom apps through vibe coding.
  • Google Career Certificates: Job-ready training across in-demand fields, including cybersecurity, data analytics, digital marketing and e-commerce, IT support, project management and UX design. Graduates of the Career Certificate program access a platform to connect directly with Google's employer consortium of more than 150 major U.S. companies, including Deloitte, Siemens, and Wells Fargo.

More than 70% of Google Career Certificate graduates report a positive career outcome within six months of completing the program, which typically takes three to six months of flexible, part-time study. Delaware residents can learn more and apply for a no-cost learning license through the Delaware Department of Labor.

entries.title: Celebrate 110 years of national parks with Maps, Search, and Gemini
entries.content:
As the U.S. heads into National Parks Week — celebrating 110 years of the National Park Service — Americans are taking their love of the outdoors to some of the country’s most iconic landmarks.

Whether you’re gearing up for your next trip or looking to satisfy your wanderlust, here’s a look at what people are searching for — and a few ways Google can help you discover, prepare for, and make the most of your next adventure.

Hit the trails

More people are hitting the trails than ever before, with overall Search interest in hiking reaching an all-time high this year. Much of that momentum is coming from newcomers: queries for “hiking for beginners” increased by 165% over the past month. As for where all these newly-minted hikers plan to start, Rocky Mountain National Park has emerged as the top trending park searched alongside “beginner hiking.”

💡Use AI Mode in Search to find the right gear for your hike. Type in exactly what you’re looking for and you’ll get options tailored to your specific needs and shoppable product listings right in your results — e.g., hiking boots with good ankle support.

Plan the big trip

Mapping out a visit to a national park can be daunting, but people are turning to Search and Google Maps for inspiration. Over the past month, Acadia National Park was the top trending national park travel itinerary on Google Search. For those looking for highly rated experiences, Haleakalā National Park and Mount Rainier National Park stand out as the top-rated national parks on Maps this year.

💡Turn your trip ideas into a shareable itinerary. Use the Gemini app to create a custom, visual invitation or packing list for your travel crew. Be specific. For example, prompt Gemini for a trip to Yellowstone National Park over Labor Day weekend and ask for a suggested list of attractions, things to pack and eat, and activities you can do, such as hiking, camping, and taking in beautiful views.

Enjoy the journey

Getting there can be just as much fun as the destination. Search interest in “how to plan a road trip” increased by 190% over the past month, with Great Sand Dunes National Park as the top trending road trip destination.

💡 Ask Maps can help you plan a memorable road trip by suggesting scenic stops, popular places to grab a bite, and giving you a heads-up on traffic delays and disruptions. You can even use it to find the perfect hotel along the way. Once you find a route that works for you, don’t forget to download your map so you can navigate even in the most remote locations.

Take in the sights

Hikers are hungry for information. Zion National Park was the most-searched national park for hikers, and its Narrows trail ranked as the top trending hike.

💡 Being surrounded by nature sparks more questions about the world in front of you, which the Gemini app is ready to help with. Tap the Live icon and click the camera to start Gemini Live. Point your lens at an unfamiliar wildflower, a distinct rock formation, or a historical trail marker, and ask Gemini what you’re looking at to get real-time insights as you hike.

Start building your bucket list by visiting United Parks of America by Google Arts & Culture, which celebrates the history and beauty of national parks. Take an interactive trip through the Everglades or discover the wildlife in Yellowstone National Park with just a click.

entries.title: How developers build AI for good with Gemma 4
entries.content:
Last week, as we celebrated one billion Gemma downloads, we shared how developers across the Gemmaverse are pushing the boundaries of open models, from spaceflight in Earth's orbit to decoding interspecies communication under the sea. But at the true heart of this thriving ecosystem is a commitment to positive impact: using AI to solve pressing human challenges.

When we kicked off the Gemma 4 Good Challenge on Kaggle, we asked the developer community to build practical AI solutions to challenges facing people around the world. The response was extraordinary, with over 1,600 submissions demonstrating that making the most of AI requires brilliant engineering. Deploying capable models in resource-constrained environments is no small feat, and developers leveraged key technologies, including LiteRT, Cactus, Ollama, llama.cpp, and Unsloth, to create highly performant solutions for everyday hardware.

Today, we celebrate our podium winners and category award recipients from across the Gemmaverse:

First Place

GEM-4 is a physical robotic assistant and control pipeline built to physically assist elderly and disabled individuals with daily living tasks. Using a Gemma 4 31B model to label video training clips, a fine-tuned, lightweight Gemma 4 E2B controller translates visual observations and language instructions into real-world physical movements. Judges lauded GEM-4 for its innovative closed-loop data engine and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architecture, creating an embodied system that moves AI reasoning directly into hands-on physical help.

Second Place

Trido enabled a voice-controlled digital whiteboard built to assist educators, particularly those with physical disabilities, in managing interactive classroom instruction. Using real-time speech processing and dual-path audio input, a locally hosted Gemma 4 E2B model dynamically generates mind maps, quizzes, and visual widgets on canvas. Judges praised its “deep user empathy and robust offline fallback loop”, creating a collaborative educational dashboard that can run on budget laptops.

Third Place

PenguinAgent is an offline-first research application and data analysis dashboard built to support wildlife ecologists conducting field expeditions in remote environments. Using Segment Anything (SAM 3) and SigLip 2 tracking inputs, a locally hosted Gemma 4 26B model ingests sequential video frames and kinematic telemetry to analyze thermodynamic huddling behavior and query local ornithological papers. Judges commended its thorough technical implementation and RAG-grounded scientific reporting, creating a local-first analysis tool that ensures complete scientific data privacy at the edge of the world.

Fourth Place

DEMENTOR is an ambient edge companion and hardware sensor network built to support individuals living with dementia. Using offline camera feeds and haptic feedback, Gemma 4 E2B helps caregivers monitor behavioral patterns and assists with daily memory retrieval. Judges highlighted its low-level hardware integration and edge orchestration, creating a system that prioritizes user safety and absolute data privacy for sensitive health metrics.

Global Resilience Prize: Acuífero·Vigía

Acuífero·Vigía is an offline-first flood early warning system deployed in South America. The system fuses local telemetry, volunteer audio descriptions, and river camera feeds to generate real-time flood predictions and localized safety instructions. Judges appreciated the project’s technical depth, specifically highlighting auditable reasoning trails for accountability and the decision to use Gemma 4 E2B to prevent WebGPU buffer overflows on Raspberry Pi 5 units.

AI Trust & Safety Prize: TrueVoice

TrueVoice tackles the rise of voice-cloning fraud, where bad actors can clone a loved one’s voice to mislead unsuspecting victims. The project leverages Gemma 4 E4B’s audio capabilities to identify voice cloning scams by analyzing vocal anomalies, emotional tones, and micro-timbres. Evaluated as a solution to a high-stakes problem, TrueVoice addresses a critical and growing threat in AI-driven fraud by deploying detection models directly to the edge, building a critical safety layer that actively intercepts scams before they can cause emotional or financial harm.

Digital Equity & Inclusion Prize: Gem-Care

Gem-Care focuses on resolving the digital exclusion of millions of people with non-normative speech in an increasingly voice-activated world. While modern Automatic Speech Recognition systems achieve high accuracy for standard speech patterns, they frequently fail for individuals with dysarthria or speech disabilities. Gem-Care fine-tuned Gemma 4 E2B to perform multimodal clinical-context adaptation, translating and reconstructing non-normative speech inputs. Judges celebrated the achievement of a Word-Error-Rate (WER) of 19.0% compared to the base model’s 32.7% WER.

Future of Education Prize: CodeBuddy

CodeBuddy helps bridge the digital divide for 28 million students in Indonesia by providing Socratic programming tutoring. Since many schools lack internet-connected computers, students write Python code in physical paper notebooks, snap a picture, and let Gemma 4 E4B transcribe, compile, and debug their code entirely offline. The judges highlighted the teacher dashboard and praised the project as a “masterclass in offline edge AI design.”

Health & Sciences Prize: Project Rosie

Project Rosie developed an agentic oncology assistant that democratizes access to personalized neoantigen mRNA cancer vaccines for canine oncology. It uses the Gemma 4 26B model to guide veterinarians through the clinical interpretation and design of personalized neoantigen mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs, while using deterministic templates for generating critical manufacturing specifications—an architectural decision praised by judges for its disciplined, non-hallucinatory design.

LiteRT Prize: Gilbeot (길벗)

Gilbeot is an on-device walking navigation assistant for elderly users. Recognizing that seniors struggle with traditional spatial mapping, Gilbeot uses local visual analysis to translate machine coordinates into human descriptions, such as turning left past a specific landmark sign. The project demonstrates exceptional performance tuning on Android devices, deploying Gemma 4 E2B via Google AI Edge’s LiteRT-LM framework to achieve fast multimodal loops without cellular service, which judges noted as a highly novel on-device walking guidance architecture.

llama.cpp Prize: PreVillage

PreVillage is a voice-first WhatsApp navigator that helps rural citizens in Nepal access government services. Using Gemma 4 E4B, it bypasses complex online government portals by using Romanized-Nepali ASR and a local RAG database to map out the undocumented routes, counters, and forms inside administrative offices. The judges hailed PreVillage as a “masterclass in user empathy and robust AI engineering,” praising its use of a self-healing RAG loop and llama.cpp execution on a Raspberry Pi 5 to serve responsive conversational routing at 7.5 tokens per second.

Ollama Prize: PathOS

PathOS is an offline histopathology screening assistant designed to bring same-day, zero-connectivity cancer detection to under-resourced rural clinics. Powered by a custom-trained Gemma 4 E2B model optimized for low-resource CPUs, the pipeline was praised by judges for its advanced reinforcement learning (GRPO) alignment to prevent clinical hedging and its complete on-device execution pipeline.

Unsloth Prize: MindBridge

MindBridge is a mental health screening tool designed to help community health workers conduct vital psychiatric evaluations in regional Hindi dialects. Built by fine-tuning Gemma 4 E2B’s native audio layers on a bespoke conversational dataset, the system was lauded by judges for its robust, TestFlight-ready mobile build, detailed on-device benchmarks, and authentic local-idiom translations.

Cactus Prize: KawanIsyarat

KawanIsyarat is an offline two-way communication assistant designed to connect deaf and hard of hearing BISINDO (Indonesian Sign Language) users. Deployed on mid-range Android smartphones, the system uses Cactus to run the Gemma 4 E2B model locally, translating camera-captured sign landmarks into natural sentences while simplifying spoken audio. The judges praised its memory-aware model routing—which dynamically loads a Whisper model for speech-to-text and unloads it to preserve VRAM for Gemma—and latency optimizations that disabled thinking mode to make real-time performance viable.

Congratulations to all participants

Over the course of six weeks, developers around the world proved what is possible when Gemma models are paired with purpose-driven engineering. From wildlife conservation at the edge to assistive robotics and healthcare diagnostics, these projects demonstrate a future for AI that is practical, accessible, and private-by-design.

As Gemma celebrates 1 billion downloads, we extend a massive thank you and congratulations to all the participants who contributed code, datasets, models, or anything else to the Gemmaverse. We can’t wait to see how these solutions mature and bring a positive impact for the world.

entries.title: What does “full-stack” AI actually mean?
entries.summary: A Google DeepMind engineer breaks full-stack development into five simple layers and explains how it affects everyday users.
entries.content:
If you’ve tried your hand at vibe coding — or even full-blown web development — you’ve probably heard the term “full-stack.” But what does it actually mean? We asked Paige Bailey, an engineering lead at Google DeepMind, to explain the concept — and how it shows up in the Google tech you use every day.

Paige helpfully breaks down full-stack development: infrastructure, security, research, models & tooling, and products. Each one serves a crucial purpose. And all five layers work together to make Google’s AI products faster, more secure, and more helpful for users, developers, and customers.

Watch the video below to see Paige’s full explanation and learn about our full-stack approach to AI.

entries.title: Here's how to use sign-to-text translation on Pixel 11.
entries.summary: Developed in partnership with the Deaf community, sign-to-text translates ASL into text in real time.
entries.content:
The brand new Pixel 11 series will bring a new sign-to-text translation feature to people who communicate using American Sign Language (ASL). Developed in partnership with the Deaf community, the new feature is powered by a multilingual sign language-to-text (SL2T) translation model. It analyzes hand shapes, facial expressions, and body movements to translate ASL into written English sentences in real time.

The feature, which supports both one-handed and two-handed signing, lets signers use their native language to express themselves when using Live Transcribe or across their device with Gboard.

To use this feature on a Pixel 11 device, add sign-to-text to your Gboard toolbar, and sign in ASL to the front camera. The translations will appear on the outer display.

The Pixel 11 series is available on shelves now. Visit the Google Store for more information on availability and product updates.
